channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Erick All was not targeted in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
item.description: Three Bengals tight ends caught at least one pass, but All somehow was not one of them. That will probably change going forward, but this is confirmation that it’s going to be a while if All is to develop back-end streamer relevance this season.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-8 targets for 48 yards in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
item.description: Week 1 was business as usual for LaPorta, who finished second on the team in catches and yards. After missing time in the offseason recovering from a season-ending back injury and later a minor hip issue, this goes down as a big win for the young tight end, even if fantasy managers aren’t thrilled with his score. LaPorta will project for TE1 numbers when the Lions take on the Ravens next week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper’s (ankle) X-rays were negative, and he will now undergo an MRI.
Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
item.description: Gesicki led the Bengals in catches, targets and yards and was the only pass catcher to score on an afternoon where the Bucs’ defense was funneling Joe Burrow to the middle of the field. Gesicki’s score was a two-yarder where he rolled in to the end zone in the first quarter. Gesicki’s yardage total would have been his second highest of 2025. He’s a valuable real-life contributor, but he is going to have trouble cracking the top 18 tight ends on a regular basis with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown all usage monsters for the Bengals.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Xavier Legette did not catch either of his two targets in Week 1 against the Bears.
item.description: Running a pass route on 28 of the team’s 42 drop backs, Legette saw two looks from Bryce Young but failed to secure either. Meanwhile, Jalen Coker went off for 138 yards and two scores and Tetairoa McMillan finished with 75 yards. Legette should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 2.-Denny Carter

item.title: Isaac TeSlaa failed to catch his only target in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
item.description: TeSlaa did his usual wind sprinting in this game and failed to bring in his only target on the day. With stars at nearly every skill position in Detroit, there simply isn’t any room for a meaningful TeSlaa role. He is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Jared Goff completed 26-of-39 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-30, Week 1 overtime win over the Saints.
item.description: Goff struggled to get much going early on this game, putting up seven points in the first half. The Lions quickly dropped 14 in the third quarter but took their foot off the gas with the Saints struggling to do much of anything. That nearly came back to bite them as Tyler Shough led a frantic comeback while the Lions amassed three points in the final frame. An overtime touchdown to Amon-Ra St. Brown proved to be just enough to come home with the win, though it required a failed two-point conversion from the Saints. Despite the slow start, Goff should return to the QB1 ranks when he squares off with the Ravens next week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Chuba Hubbard had ten rushes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 38 yards and a touchdown.
item.description: Hubbard was the clearcut lead back for the run-heavy Carolina offense. Jonathon Brooks saw five touches on the day, and ran six pass routes for 29 routes for Hubbard, who was the Panthers’ primary red zone back throughout the game. For now Hubbard’s role in the run-first Panthers offense seems secure while the team eases Brooks into action. That could change at some point this season. Hubbard will be a locked-in RB2 option next week against a middling Falcons defense.-Denny Carter

item.title: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
item.description: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 1 against the Eagles.
item.description: Okonkwo exited in the third quarter, and at the start of the fourth quarter, it was revealed that the Commanders’ TE1 would be questionable to return. Okonkwo has caught two passes for 16 yards so far, as the Commanders have struggled to generate much through the air.-Zachary Krueger
